procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Patna
procedural_history.impugned_order: Order dated 25.07.2023 of the High Court of Judicature at Patna in Criminal Miscellaneous No. 28525 of 2023, granting anticipatory bail to respondents nos. 2 to 4.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court granted anticipatory bail to respondents nos. 2 to 4 in Criminal Miscellaneous No. 28525 of 2023.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant-complainant appealed the High Court's order granting anticipatory bail, arguing it was unwarranted given the specific allegations of a heinous crime (Section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860) and the chargesheet on record. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, and directed respondents nos. 2 to 4 to surrender before the Trial Court.

directions: The impugned order of the High Court dated 25.07.2023 is set aside.

Respondent nos. 2 to 4 are directed to surrender before the Trial Court within four weeks from today and they are granted liberty to file an application for regular bail, which if filed would be considered as per law on its own merits uninfluenced by any observations made in this judgment.

issue.issue_text: Whether the High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail to accused persons despite specific allegations of heinous crime u/s.302 of Penal Code, 1860 and chargesheet on record that established the allegations made u/s.302 of Penal Code, 1860 are true.

facts: The accused (respondents) were implicated in a case involving a heinous crime under Section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 (murder).
The First Information Report (FIR) contained specific allegations that the accused set the deceased on fire with an intention to kill.
A chargesheet was filed by the police which stated that the allegations of murder were found to be true against all the accused persons.
The accused were initially denied anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court.
Subsequently, the High Court granted anticipatory bail to the accused, which was then challenged in the Supreme Court by the complainant.
law: The grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of judicial discretion that must be exercised carefully, not in a mechanical manner.

Citing the precedent in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi), the Court reiterated that when deciding on anticipatory bail, a court must consider factors such as the nature and gravity of the offense, the role attributed to the accused, and the specific facts of the case.
application: The Supreme Court found that the High Court failed to properly apply the established legal principles for granting anticipatory bail.
The High Court did not account for the heinous nature and gravity of the offense, which involved murder by setting a person on fire.
It ignored the specific averments against the accused in the FIR and the findings in the police chargesheet, which supported the allegations.
The Supreme Court characterized the High Court's order as "cryptic and mechanical," meaning it was passed without proper consideration of the materials on record and lacked sufficient reasoning.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail. Given the specific allegations, the evidence in the chargesheet, and the serious nature of the murder offense, the Supreme Court deemed it inappropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the accused and set aside the High Court's order.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail to accused persons despite specific allegations of heinous crime u/s.302 of Penal Code, 1860 and chargesheet on record that established the allegations made u/s.302 of Penal Code, 1860 are true.
appellant_arguments: The High Court's grant of anticipatory bail was unwarranted.
The High Court failed to consider relevant aspects of the case and disregarded the evidence on record.
Bail should not have been granted given the specific allegations of a heinous crime (murder under Section 302, IPC) and the fact that a chargesheet on record established the allegations as true.
respondent_arguments: The provided text does not contain any arguments from the respondents. It is noted that the respondents (accused persons) initially failed to appear, and later instructed their counsel not to appear on their behalf anymore.

cases.case_name: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
cases.principle: Courts ought to be guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant or refuse anticipatory bail.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The grant of anticipatory bail in cases involving heinous offenses requires a careful and considered evaluation of the materials on record, the gravity of the offense, and the specific role of the accused; granting such relief in a cryptic and mechanical manner, without due consideration of these factors, is an improper exercise of judicial discretion.
obiter: Issuing non-bailable warrants is appropriate to ensure the appearance of accused persons who are evading appearance before the Supreme Court, even after being served notice.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail to the accused in a case involving a heinous offense under Section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860. The High Court granted relief in a cryptic and mechanical manner despite specific averments in the FIR about the heinous nature of the crime (setting the deceased on fire with an intention to kill) and a chargesheet stating that the allegations were found to be true against all the accused.
legal_tests_applied: Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it. Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion; equally whether and if so, what kind of special conditions are to be imposed (or not imposed) are dependent on facts of the case, and subject to the discretion of the court.
policy_considerations: Grant of anticipatory bail in such serious offenses requires careful consideration of the materials on record, the gravity of the offense, and the role of the accused.
